definitions: A technique used in computer graphics, particularly in rendering, to resolve or mitigate issues where objects might incorrectly cast shadows on themselves or other objects due to rendering artifacts or specific lighting setups.

A method employed to ensure that all parts of a scene are appropriately lit and not inadvertently obscured by self-shadowing or other unintended shadow effects, often involving adjustments to shadow mapping or lighting algorithms.
examples: The developer implemented the Global Unshadowing Trick to fix the flickering shadows.
Without the Global Unshadowing Trick, the character's arm would incorrectly shadow its own body.
Applying the Global Unshadowing Trick improved the visual quality of the rendered scene significantly.
